name: Free Software Foundation — license list
trustNote: The FSF wrote the GPL, LGPL and AGPL. Its license list is the last word on whether a license is GPL-compatible and whether the FSF considers it a free software license. It is not the authority on whether a license is 'open source' (that is the OSI).

name: GNU Licenses FAQ
trustNote: Explains linking, plugins, static vs dynamic linking, 'or later' versioning, and AGPL network use for the GPL family. Prefer it over blog posts and Stack Overflow answers.

name: Open Source Initiative — approved licenses
trustNote: Only the OSI decides whether a license is 'OSI approved' / 'open source'. OSI approval does not imply GPL compatibility, and the OSI has approved licenses the FSF does not call free (e.g. Artistic-1.0, NASA-1.3).

name: SPDX License List
trustNote: Canonical short identifiers and expression syntax (AND / OR / WITH). Its isOsiApproved and isFsfLibre flags mirror the OSI and FSF lists; SPDX itself takes no position on compatibility.

name: Apache Software Foundation — GPL compatibility
trustNote: Steward of Apache-2.0. Authoritative on what the ASF itself will accept into Apache projects (third-party licensing policy) and on the ASF's reading of Apache-2.0 vs GPL.

name: Apache Software Foundation — third-party license policy
trustNote: Category A / B / X lists: which licenses ASF projects may include. Useful as a conservative corporate-style policy; not a statement about legality outside the ASF.

name: Mozilla — MPL 2.0 FAQ
trustNote: Steward of MPL-2.0. Authoritative on the file-level copyleft scope and the Secondary License (GPL/LGPL/AGPL) compatibility clause.

name: Eclipse Foundation — EPL 2.0 FAQ
trustNote: Steward of EPL-2.0. Authoritative on the optional GPL-2.0 Secondary License designation (Exhibit A) and module-level copyleft scope.

name: choosealicense.com (GitHub)
trustNote: Plain-language permissions / conditions / limitations, MIT-licensed data. Good for summaries; not a legal authority and it says nothing about compatibility.

name: Blue Oak Council — model license list
trustNote: Steward of the Blue Oak Model License 1.0.0. The FSF license list does not mention Blue Oak licenses at all; use this and the OSI/ASF listings, not an absent FSF verdict, for Blue Oak questions.

name: GitHub Docs — Licensing a repository
trustNote: Explains the default: public code without a license is all rights reserved. Not an authority on any specific license.
